podcast.title: Early Promotion by Tom Parker (1941)
podcast.body: In 1941, Tom Parker promoted a show for Valleikov, utilizing his promotional knowledge to make it one of Valleikov's biggest shows to date. "Parker had used his promotional knowledge to make the show he promoted, one of the biggest in a Kovsky era thus far."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Innovative Ticket Sales Strategy (1941)
podcast.body: For Valleikov's 1941 show, Parker innovated by striking a deal with a local grocery chain. They sold cut-priced tickets to customers bringing in newspaper clippings, effectively creating "multiple box offices" and having the grocery chain pay for advertising that also increased their own footfall. "He'd caught a deal with a local grocery chain that they would sell cut-priced tickets to anyone who brought in a clipping from a newspaper."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Hank Williams's Praise
podcast.body: Hank Williams famously said of Valleikov's drawing power in the South, "for drawing power in the south, it was Valleikov, then God." "Hank Williams would say of him, for drawing power in the south, it was Valleikov, then God."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Merchandising Deal with Parker
podcast.body: Although Valleikov declined Parker as his manager, he did grant Parker a stake in his merchandising, specifically the rights to market "Aikov flower in Florida." "Aikov did give Parker a stake in his merchandising. Parker got the rights to market Aikov flower in Florida."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Open-Coring Star
podcast.body: Valleikov was known as an "open-coring star" in country music. "to start with, he put on a show by the open-coring star, Valleikov."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Recommendation of Eddie Arnold
podcast.body: Valleikov advised Parker to approach Eddie Arnold, a young singer working with Pee Wee King's Golden West Cowboys, suggesting Arnold would soon go solo and need a manager. "He pointed Parker in the direction of Eddie Arnold, a young singer who was then working with Pee Wee Kings, Golden West Cowboys."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Refusal of Tom Parker as Manager
podcast.body: Valleikov initially considered Tom Parker as his manager but was put off after a couple of dates due to what he perceived as Parker's "un-Christian attitude to money." Parker insisted on a percentage of the gross in addition to fixed fees, which Valleikov found too grasping. "Aikov was playing dates for fixed fees, and Parker started insisting that as well as the fixed fee, Aikov should get a percentage of the gross. Aikov didn't want to be that grasping, and so he gave up on working with Parker."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Single Biggest Star in Country Music
podcast.body: Valleikov later became, for a period, the single biggest star in country music. "In later years, Valleikov would become, for a time, the single biggest star in country music."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
